verdicts.reason: Candidate provides no substantive analysis and does not identify the boat insurance contract as the maritime contract at issue.
Candidate does not identify New York law as the contractually selected law.
Candidate does not distinguish the Pennsylvania federal litigation from the contractual choice of New York law.
Candidate does not identify the grounding near Fort Lauderdale, Florida.
Candidate does not identify the alleged failure to maintain the fire-suppression system.
Candidate does not recognize that the alleged fire-suppression breach did not contribute to the grounding.
Candidate does not label complete-policy voidance as Great Lakes’ asserted position rather than a Supreme Court coverage holding.
Candidate does not identify the Third Circuit’s forum-public-policy exception and remand approach.
Candidate does not apply federal maritime law to the enforceability of the choice-of-law clause.
Candidate does not state the federal maritime presumption of enforceability for choice-of-law clauses.
Candidate does not explain the maritime uniformity interest.
Candidate does not explain advance certainty and predictability for maritime contracting parties.
Candidate does not address freedom of contract or settled expectations supporting enforcement.
Candidate does not use the forum-selection cases while keeping forum and law clauses distinct.
Candidate does not distinguish Wilburn Boat’s lack of a substantive federal warranty rule from the federal enforceability rule for choice-of-law clauses.
Candidate does not recognize that state substantive law may govern after the federal choice rule selects it.
Candidate does not identify conflict with a controlling federal statute as an enforceability exception.
Candidate does not identify conflict with established federal maritime policy as an enforceability exception.
Candidate does not recognize the no-reasonable-basis exception.
Candidate does not address the substantial deference owed to the parties in the reasonable-basis inquiry.
Candidate does not recognize that well-developed commercial law may provide a rational basis for choosing New York law.
Candidate does not recognize that Raiders failed to assert the recognized federal-conflict or no-reasonable-basis exceptions.
Candidate does not explain the rejection of an additional fundamental forum-state public-policy exception.
Candidate does not explain why Restatement §187(2)(b) was not adopted for federal maritime law.
Candidate does not state that the Third Circuit judgment was reversed.
Candidate does not separate enforceability of the choice clause from final policy coverage or damages.
Candidate does not attribute criticism of Wilburn Boat to Justice Thomas’s separate concurrence.
Candidate does not fairly present the insured’s Pennsylvania-policy contention before its rejection.
Candidate does not request or verify the full policy, endorsements, or federal-law priority before clause-specific advice.
Candidate does not request the warranty text, maintenance evidence, denial grounds, and loss facts for remaining coverage analysis.
Candidate does not tie any remaining enforceability challenge to evidence of a recognized federal-conflict or reasonable-basis exception.
Candidate does not separate likely application of New York law from a conditional coverage outcome under the full policy and record.
